questions.question: In a standard 2D convolutional layer with kernel size k×k, how can the weights for a single output channel be interpreted at a high level?
questions.choice_A: As a set of channel-wise neuron vectors, one k×k spatial kernel per input channel whose responses are summed to produce that output channel
questions.choice_B: As a single k×k spatial kernel shared across all input channels without any channel-specific parameters
questions.choice_C: As a fully connected matrix applied to the flattened input feature map at each layer
questions.choice_D: As a depthwise operation that never mixes information across input channels

questions.question: Which statement best describes depthwise separable convolutions?
questions.choice_A: They use a single large kernel to replace multiple small kernels, increasing parameter efficiency
questions.choice_B: They factor a standard convolution into a depthwise spatial convolution applied per input channel followed by a 1×1 pointwise convolution to mix channels
questions.choice_C: They only reduce compute when the stride is larger than one
questions.choice_D: They are identical to grouped convolutions with two groups

questions.question: In Transformer attention, what is the primary role of the value (V) projection?
questions.choice_A: To produce scores that determine which tokens attend to each other
questions.choice_B: To normalize attention weights before softmax
questions.choice_C: To carry the content vectors that are linearly combined according to the attention weights
questions.choice_D: To map multi-head outputs back to the embedding dimension

questions.question: Where are lightweight adapters most commonly inserted in Transformer layers for parameter-efficient finetuning while preserving the base model?
questions.choice_A: Only before the input embedding layer to reduce sequence length
questions.choice_B: Inside the softmax operation to modify attention sparsity
questions.choice_C: Exclusively on layer normalization parameters to adjust scaling
questions.choice_D: After linear projections in attention (Q/K/V/O) and within the MLP (often between up- and down-projections), connected via residual paths

questions.question: How is per-neuron parameterization realized in a fully connected (MLP) layer?
questions.choice_A: Each output neuron has a distinct weight vector over the input and its own bias
questions.choice_B: All output neurons share weights but use different biases
questions.choice_C: Weights are tied across both inputs and outputs to reduce dimensionality
questions.choice_D: Each output neuron is defined only by a bias term without weights

questions.question: For best quality per trained parameter in large language models, LoRA-style low-rank adapters are often applied to which matrices?
questions.choice_A: Only the output embedding matrix
questions.choice_B: Attention projections (Q, K, V, and output projection) and sometimes MLP up/down projections
questions.choice_C: Exclusively to layer normalization gain and bias
questions.choice_D: Only to positional encoding parameters

questions.question: What is the main motivation for low-rank adaptations (e.g., LoRA) when finetuning large models?
questions.choice_A: They eliminate the need for backpropagation
questions.choice_B: They guarantee zero-shot performance will never degrade
questions.choice_C: They capture the dominant update directions with far fewer trainable parameters and lower memory bandwidth
questions.choice_D: They remove the need for any optimizer hyperparameter tuning

questions.question: Compared to a standard convolution with Cin input and Cout output channels, which design significantly reduces parameters when Cout is large while preserving accuracy?
questions.choice_A: Using larger kernels with more padding
questions.choice_B: Replacing convolutions with average pooling layers
questions.choice_C: Increasing dilation to cover larger receptive fields
questions.choice_D: Using depthwise separable convolutions to decouple spatial filtering (per-channel) from channel mixing (1×1)

questions.question: Why might one constrain adapter weights to be orthogonal or near-orthogonal to the base features?
questions.choice_A: To preserve norms and act as near-rotations that minimally distort pretrained representations while enabling task-specific changes
questions.choice_B: To reduce the need for residual connections in deep networks
questions.choice_C: To make the adapters exactly equivalent to low-rank updates
questions.choice_D: To ensure the attention matrix remains strictly positive definite

questions.question: If the goal is to modulate which tokens attend to which, which projections are the most direct targets for adapters?
questions.choice_A: Only the output projection after multi-head concatenation
questions.choice_B: The query and key projections, because they shape the attention score distribution
questions.choice_C: The value projection, because it rescales content after softmax
questions.choice_D: The positional encodings, because they determine token identity

questions.question: Conceptually, how should a 1×1 convolution be viewed in relation to channel-wise parameterization?
questions.choice_A: As a spatial smoothing filter with no channel mixing
questions.choice_B: As a replacement for max pooling that reduces spatial size
questions.choice_C: As a linear transformation across channels at each spatial location, mixing per-location channel vectors
questions.choice_D: As a transposed convolution that upsamples feature maps

questions.question: What is a typical outcome of finetuning only biases and LayerNorm parameters (e.g., BitFit-style tuning)?
questions.choice_A: Performance identical to full-model finetuning on all tasks
questions.choice_B: Severe overfitting due to excessive capacity
questions.choice_C: Inability to learn any task-specific behavior
questions.choice_D: Modest gains with very low memory/compute overhead, often preserving base model behavior

questions.question: In Transformer MLP blocks with an up-projection and down-projection, where do multiplicative-rescaling adapters like IA3 typically act?
questions.choice_A: As learned per-channel scaling vectors on value projections and on the intermediate (expanded) MLP channels
questions.choice_B: Only on the output embedding to steer token probabilities
questions.choice_C: Exclusively inside the GELU activation to change its shape
questions.choice_D: On positional encodings to change effective sequence length

questions.question: Why might a 1×1 pointwise convolution be preferred over a fully connected layer applied to flattened spatial features when mixing channels?
questions.choice_A: Because it increases the number of trainable parameters for better capacity
questions.choice_B: Because it shares weights across spatial locations, preserving spatial structure with fewer parameters and lower memory
questions.choice_C: Because it eliminates the need for non-linearities in the network
questions.choice_D: Because it can replace attention mechanisms entirely

questions.question: Which finetuning choice primarily adjusts task-specific decision boundaries without substantially altering internal representations?
questions.choice_A: Training only the positional encodings
questions.choice_B: Training only layer normalization parameters
questions.choice_C: Training only the final classification/output head
questions.choice_D: Training only the key and query projections

questions.question: When inserting low-rank adapters into attention to avoid changing the quadratic sequence-length component of compute, which placement is preferable?
questions.choice_A: Directly modifying the attention score matrix after softmax
questions.choice_B: Inside the softmax so that rank constraints apply to probability vectors
questions.choice_C: Only on the positional encodings to reduce length dependence
questions.choice_D: As low-rank updates to the linear projections (Q, K, V, O) rather than to the score computation itself

questions.question: Increasing the number of output channels in a standard convolution primarily does what in terms of representation capacity?
questions.choice_A: Adds more learned patterns (filters) per spatial location, akin to adding more neurons that detect different features
questions.choice_B: Only increases receptive field size without adding parameters
questions.choice_C: Decreases the computational cost per forward pass
questions.choice_D: Eliminates the need for non-linear activations

questions.question: Where are residual, bottleneck-style adapters usually placed within a Transformer block to minimize interference with pretrained representations?
questions.choice_A: Before the token embedding lookup
questions.choice_B: After the attention output projection and after the MLP, each inside the corresponding residual branch
questions.choice_C: Between layer normalization and positional encoding addition
questions.choice_D: Inside the softmax of the attention mechanism

questions.question: How does grouped convolution compare to depthwise convolution in terms of channel mixing?
questions.choice_A: Grouped convolution mixes all channels together like a standard convolution
questions.choice_B: Grouped convolution uses no channel mixing at all, like a depthwise convolution
questions.choice_C: Depthwise convolution is the extreme case of grouped convolution where the number of groups equals the number of input channels
questions.choice_D: There is no relationship; they are different operations

questions.question: In practice, when might orthogonally constrained low-rank adapters be preferred over unconstrained ones?
questions.choice_A: When the base model is randomly initialized and has no prior structure
questions.choice_B: When you want the adapters to exactly emulate full fine-tuning
questions.choice_C: When compute is abundant but memory is extremely limited
questions.choice_D: When you want to stabilize finetuning by applying near-rotational updates that reduce interference with pretrained features
